newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open flat-down, durables to set tone.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open flat-down, durables to set tone.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries opened flat to a touch weaker on Friday, with this morning's report on durable goods expected to give the market early direction.
The 30-year bond was at 102-13/32, down 1/32, to yield 6.44 percent.
After both buying and selling in overseas trading during the night, players said durable goods data, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, will set the tone this session.
Durable goods orders were expected to show a 1.4 percent rise in June, after falling 0.7 percent in May, according to a Reuters poll of economists.
"It's (only) durable goods and hopefully we can call it a day around noontime," said Jim Stewart, senior trader at Yamaichi International (America) Inc, half-jokingly.

Traders said that no matter what the data show, the market is in a trend to higher prices. "We have plenty of people under the market," Stewart said. "There is nothing in the cards that will push prices down -- unless we get a string of strong economic numbers."

Earlier in London, Treasuries fell, with the bond down as low as 102-10/32 following another wave of hedge fund selling, which was also seen in New York on Thursday. That followed buying in Tokyo which took the bond up to 102-18/32.
In recent sessions, foreign buying has helped the market offset selling from hedge funds.
Much of the buying has been in intermediate and longer dated paper, which has resulted in a continued flattening of the yield curve.
Most market participants said they did not anticipate a breakout from the fairly narrow ranges seen in recent days.

Traders said that should the September bond contract move above the 115-20 or so level -- a double top -- it could prompt another rally of a half-point. On the flip side, the contract is said to have strong support at around 114-25/32. If that breaks, a move to the low 114s is seen likely, traders predicted.
In early trading, the September contract was at 115-6/32, down 4/32.

The cash two-year note was unchanged at 100 to yield 5.86 percent. The five-year note was unchanged at 99-23/32 to yield 6.07 percent, while the 10-year note was unchanged at at 103-12/32 to yield 6.16 percent.
Three-month, six-month and year bills were also unchanged at 5.08, 5.14 and 5.22 percent, respectively.
